newsitem.title: UK: BT says no comment on MCI until after review.
newsitem.headline: BT says no comment on MCI until after review.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc said on Wednesday it could not make any promises about the future of its ambitious merger plan with MCI Communications ahead of a full-scale review of the U.S. carrier's prospects.

Speaking before a crucial annual meeting of BT shareholders in the wake of an unexpected profit warning by MCI last week rocked the $20 billion-plus merger, BT confirmed that a review would be headed by the two companies' chief executives, Sir Peter Bonfield and Gerry Taylor.
"Until such a time as the review is completed, we cannot comment on the future of this merger," a BT spokesman told Reuters.
Asked how long the investigation, in which BT finance director Robert Brace is likely to take on the number crunching, would take, the spokesman said, "How long is a piece of string?"
The review is likely to start immediately after the shareholder meeting, with Bonfield set to fly to the U.S. over the bext few days.
"It's a matter of great urgency, and our shareholders want to know what is going on...We will make a statement when we have something to say," the spokesman said.
MCI said last week that it expected to ring up substantially larger than expected losses in entering local U.S. markets, blaming foot-dragging by local monopoly U.S. operators.
Despite the problems of gaining access to these potentially lucrative marekts, America's second biggest long-distance carrier MCI said it planned to substantially step up investment.
MCI warned of an additional $500 million losses this year and an extra $700 million to $1billion in 1998.

BT, which has been under pressure from insitutional shareholers to investigate whether the terms of the merger should be renegotiated after a sharp fall in the companies' share prices, says there may be other and cheaper ways of entering local U.S. markets.

But the company denied a report in the Wall Street Journal that changes in MCI's local U.S. business could not be considered a "material adverse" event and thus be grounds to prompt new terms for the deal.
BT has also denied that MCI shareholders received early warnings in March of problems breaking into local markets that were not disclosed to BT.
BT says it first heard of the new forecast losses last Wednesday, and promptly issued a statement to its own shareholders the following day.
MCI chairman Bert Roberts, who is a director of BT, will be attending what is expected to be a stormy shareholder meeting, due to start at 0930 GMT, along with Sir Iain Vallance of BT.
